accuracy.evidence: Rules checked against the RLSS UK / RNLI Water Safety Code (Stop and think, Stay together, Float, call 999 or 112), RNLI Float to Live (lean back, spread arms and legs to stay stable, then call for help or swim to safety), RNLI beach flag meanings (red and yellow = lifeguarded area to swim between; red = danger, no swimming) and RNLI / RLSS advice on helping someone in trouble (call for help, throw something that floats, do not go in). Curriculum codes checked in the PSHE Association Programme of Study KS1 (2020): H29 risk in everyday situations, H32 keeping safe at a beach or swimming pool, H36 getting help in an emergency.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips the adult text names: 'I swim well so I can go alone' (prediction and the strong-swimmer card refused), a friend counting as a grown-up, a calm lake looking safe, swimming behind rocks, far out or by the red flag (each refused with its own reason), running on a wet poolside (a fast drag makes the child slip), jumping in at the deep end, jumping in to rescue (refused: they can pull you under) and thrashing instead of floating.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagwatersafe is built on water-specific mechanics: a Go in / Wait decision about who is watching, dragging a swimmer onto a drawn beach where only spots between the red and yellow flags and in sight are accepted, a poolside walk where drag speed is measured and a fast drag makes the child slip, a rescue where the ring float must be dragged close enough to reach Sam after shouting for help, and a starfish float built limb by limb. It does not reuse 1046 flaggetout (fire escape) or 211 (general safety rules); the 6-token shingle gate reports no flag lab above 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers each rule by acting: the strong-swimmer card bounces out of Go in, the swimmer dropped behind the rocks gets 'your grown-up cannot see you', a fast drag on the wet floor tips the child over and sends them back to the door, a short ring throw misses Sam, throwing before shouting is stopped with 'Shout for a grown-up first', and the float only reads 'Steady' once the head is back and all four limbs are spread. Each DONE line states the rule.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: 'Yes, I swim well' (the strong-swimmer card is refused), 'By the red flag' / 'Anywhere in the sea' for where lifeguards watch (the beach refuses the red-flag and deep-water spots), and 'Yes, jump in and pull Sam out' (the Jump in card is refused and the ring rescue works).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions checked in the browser with chal.cjs; every wrong option has its own slip message: strong, friend, red, rocks, jump ('Someone in trouble can pull you under too'), hide, keep ('The ring helps only if it is in the water with your friend'), thrash, tuck, run ('Slip! The floor is wet') and deep ('Go in by the steps, at the shallow end').

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are short sentences in everyday words for a 6 to 7 year old or a grown-up reading aloud (Flesch-Kincaid 1.0, family kid limit 5.0); lab cards are a few words each with drawn flags, pool and figures. The adult text (7.3, limit 10.0) names the precise terms: trusted adult, lifeguarded area, red and yellow flags, shallow and deep end, Float to Live.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph covers one rule (who must be there, where to swim, the poolside, helping and floating). Adult paragraphs give the curriculum codes and sources, why each belief is unsafe, the named mistakes, and what to practise and what the lab does. The content gate finds no filler phrase.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px phone screenshots in light and dark for all five scenes: situation cards wrap inside the card above the two tall boxes whose ticked lists fit, beach spots are large dashed circles with ✓ / ✗ chips at the centre clear of the flags, the poolside child and steps stay inside the canvas with the two choice cards side by side, the help scene keeps the action cards above the edge with You and Grown-up chips apart, and the starfish target circles sit clear of the Kick card.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Go in / Wait naming the situation, one Swim here button per beach spot, Walk a step / Run and both ways in, Shout / Throw the ring / Jump in, and one button per body part plus Kick and splash. The canvas aria-label carries each scene description and every piece of feedback; challenge feedback is a role=status live region; right and wrong carry ✓ and ✗ as well as colour; axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes.
